## Repository defaults

- Solution format: `.slnx` by default; use legacy `.sln` only when an external tool or project requirement requires it.
- Repository-level `Directory.Build.props` holds genuinely shared .NET build settings and `Directory.Packages.props` holds Central Package Management versions; project-specific settings stay in their owning projects.
- Physical layout: backend production and test projects under `backend/<Name>.<Layer>/`, the Angular workspace under `frontend/<Name>.Web/`, maintained documentation under `docs/`. Keep them clearly separated and do not create a separate top-level `tests/` directory. Project mapping: `layout.md`.

Read `.claude/rules/0-core/dependency-hygiene.md` and `.claude/rules/3-project/package-management.md` (they may not have loaded). Confirm that the change needs the package now, that the approved stack (`3-project/decisions.md`) does not already cover the need, and that it is not a Reserved addition (CLAUDE.md → Decision control). Approved conditional packages are added only when their trigger condition holds.

Policy owners: bounded execution time, retry safety, Retry-After, fallback semantics, caller cancellation → `.claude/rules/0-core/runtime-principles.md`; package choice and the direct-Polly exception → `add-dependency`; approved conditional packages → `3-project/decisions.md`. Resilience policies must match failure and operation semantics; do not add mechanisms merely because they are available.
Add baseline packages only for capabilities present in the initial project, each through `add-dependency` (versions resolved at install time). Conditional packages wait for their trigger.

When the project uses Angular Material, use its components consistently for common UI primitives; do not wrap every Material component in a custom abstraction without a concrete reason.

## Generated API clients

When OpenAPI client generation is adopted: treat generated code as generated, keep it separate from handwritten feature logic, regenerate it when the contract changes, and do not patch generated files unless the generation workflow requires it (`swagger` skill for contract concerns).

## Testing

Useful targets: meaningful component behavior, validation, data-access request mapping, important route/auth behavior, complex reactive state. Do not test framework internals or duplicate the same behavior at every level. E2E tests (Playwright, when adopted) focus on a small number of important user workflows unless broader coverage is required.

When frontend scope exists, create it with the current Angular CLI under `frontend/<Name>.Web/` (for example `npx @angular/cli@latest new <Name>.Web --directory frontend/<Name>.Web --routing --style=scss --strict`, plus `--zoneless` when the CLI version offers it), using the baseline in `decisions.md` and letting the CLI select compatible Angular/TypeScript/RxJS versions. Do not impose an obsolete directory structure on what the current CLI generates; feature structure follows `frontend-structure.md`.
